subject: Perf baseline exec visibility (Q1'26) — make baseline a release requirement
body:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Jan 10, 2026 at 9:14 AM
Subject: Perf baseline exec visibility (Q1'26) — make baseline a release requirement

Mateo + Sean,

I want to align on making the Q1 perf baseline suite a formal runtime release requirement (not just “nice-to-have”). I’m getting questions from Product + a couple enterprise threads about whether our published/internal numbers are stable across releases.

Proposal:
1) Any runtime release candidate must run the baseline suite for the “top served” models + traffic shapes (Q1 list).
2) Results must be attached to the release checklist, with pass/fail criteria per the perf regression policy.
3) In Q1 we can phase this in: warn-only gate in CI + nightly baseline in perf-canary → then release-blocking for RCs.

Asks / what I need from you both:
- Mateo: can we agree this is a hard requirement for runtime releases starting Feb (Week 6-ish of the plan), with exception process only?
- Sean: do you have an SRE owner bandwidth for the nightly baseline reliability + rerun runbook? I think this needs at least 0.5 FTE for Q1 to avoid “it’s red, but nobody knows why” churn.

I’m referencing:
- ENG-4821 (parent initiative)
- ENG-4833 (release qualification checklist update)
- Perf regression policy draft in Confluence (perf-regression-policy-q1-2026)

If you’re both aligned, I’ll schedule a 30-min checkpoint next week to lock: (a) what’s mandatory for RCs vs “nice”, (b) who signs off when a baseline moves, (c) timeline for warn-only → blocking.

Thanks,
Ava

—
Ava Chen
Program Management
Redwood Inference



From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Jan 10, 2026 at 11:02 AM
Subject: Re: Perf baseline exec visibility (Q1'26) — make baseline a release requirement

Agree with the direction.

Two constraints to be explicit about:
- We need a defined “variance budget” + enforcement that the fleet env is pinned (driver/CUDA/runtime build metadata). Otherwise we’ll block releases on noise.
- The first two weeks need to stay focused on defining the workload suite + measurement definitions (TTFT/TPOT, streaming edge cases, etc.).

But yes: by the time we have Run 1 locked, baselines should be part of RC qualification.

Let’s define:
- RC requirement: baseline suite run (subset), results attached, with clear “pass” criteria.
- PR requirement: smaller perf smoke (warn-only) to catch obvious regressions.

Sean — can you weigh in on SRE ownership? We’ll also need help with paging criteria (what wakes someone vs what’s triaged next day).

Mateo

—
Mateo Alvarez
VP Engineering, Runtime
Redwood Inference



From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 12, 2026 at 8:41 AM
Subject: Re: Perf baseline exec visibility (Q1'26) — make baseline a release requirement

I’m supportive, with a couple operational guardrails.

SRE resourcing:
- I can allocate one SRE (not full-time) for Q1 to own the nightly job health + rerun procedures, but we’ll need Runtime/ObsEng to own “why did it regress” investigations.
- For paging: only page if (a) the runner is broken for >24h, or (b) we see a severe regression across multiple regions/hardware AND it meets the policy threshold.

To Mateo’s point: we must enforce env pinning and stamp build metadata into outputs. Otherwise we’ll spend the quarter chasing driver drift.

If we’re making this a release requirement, I want:
1) A formal runbook (how to rerun, how to mark a run invalid, where artifacts live)
2) A single “baseline status” dashboard with links to the exact commit SHA + runner version + fleet SKU
3) A clear escalation path when a release candidate fails the gate (who decides to rollback vs accept with exception)

Ava — happy to join a 30-min checkpoint. I’d also recommend we explicitly pick a “go/no-go” date for when it becomes release-blocking.

Sean

—
Sean Gallagher
SRE Lead
Redwood Inference



From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 12, 2026 at 10:03 AM
Subject: Re: Perf baseline exec visibility (Q1'26) — make baseline a release requirement

This is great — thank you.

On “go/no-go” date: can we target Feb 20 as the point where RCs must attach a baseline run (even if PR gate is still warn-only)? That roughly lines up with the project timeline (Weeks 6–8: execute baseline runs; lock artifacts).

Concrete proposal for Q1:
- By Jan 30: ENG-4833 updated checklist drafted + reviewed (Connor/Sahana looped separately).
- By Feb 13: nightly baseline pipeline stable (ENG-4827), with runbook and failure classification.
- Feb 20: baseline suite required for runtime RCs (release-blocking).
- March: PR-level perf smoke remains warn-only, but visible and tracked.

Open item: who is the “sign-off” group for baseline movement? My draft is:
- Runtime (Mateo delegate) + SRE (Sean delegate) + Applied ML methodology (Jonas or Sana) for any baseline refresh / rule change.

Sean — for the SRE you can allocate: can you send me the name once confirmed so I can add them to the weekly status + ensure they’re on the pager rotation for the job (not for perf regressions).

Mateo — does Feb 20 RC gating feel realistic from a runtime-side? If not, I’d rather pick a later date now than slip repeatedly.

Ava



From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 13, 2026 at 1:27 PM
Subject: Re: Perf baseline exec visibility (Q1'26) — make baseline a release requirement

Feb 20 as “RC must have baseline attached” is realistic IF:
- The workload suite is locked by end of Week 2 (no churn after that unless it’s a bug fix).
- The runner emits stamped metadata (runtime SHA, CUDA/driver, instance type) and we enforce it.

I’m OK with release-blocking on RCs starting Feb 20, with an explicit exception workflow:
- Exception requires Runtime + SRE sign-off (Applied ML only required if it’s changing methodology / workload).
- Exceptions must be documented in the release notes (internal) with rationale.

Re sign-off group for baseline moves: I agree with your proposed trio, but I’d keep it lightweight. Most changes should be “no baseline move” by default.

Also: I want a weekly checkpoint on variance and fleet drift until we stabilize.

Mateo



From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 14, 2026 at 4:37 PM
Subject: Re: Perf baseline exec visibility (Q1'26) — make baseline a release requirement

Works for me.

SRE owner: I’m assigning Vanessa Ortiz as the primary point for the nightly baseline job + environment drift controls. She’ll coordinate with whoever is owning fleet normalization work.

Additional guardrail I’d like in the checklist (ENG-4833):
- If the baseline run is “invalid” due to env drift (e.g., driver mismatch), it must be rerun; can’t be used to pass an RC.

Ava — go ahead and schedule the checkpoint. Suggested agenda:
1) Feb 20 gating scope (which models/shapes are required for RC)
2) Paging + rerun policy (what is actionable vs noise)
3) Exception workflow + sign-offs
4) Dashboard links + artifact retention location

Sean
